why: True for createBox and the other shape factories as probed, but 'no factory assigns one' is false: createLines (src/mesh/create-line-system.ts) assigns a line material.

The probe shows each missing step (link, casters, shadow-support registration, early receiveShadows) removes the map draw or the sampling, and receiveShadows set late stayed unpicked even after ten frames and markMeshRenderableDirty.
The probe shows the hide/show cascade, the camera skip and the retire-then-throw path, and a grandchild added with setParent was hidden too.
The probe shows all three ways of parenting as described, and setParent also kept the world position under a rotated and scaled pivot.

The probe shows the tracked setters, the untracked plain writes, the hemispheric bump and the spot angle; a point light's position.set was uploaded and setLightDiffuseColor on a hemispheric light throws.

The probe shows the origin-light depth fault and the thin-instance bounds rule, but the fixed 'back 50 units' step does not cover all casters: a caster 10 units upstream of that light position got depth below 0 and fell out of the map.
The probe shows the kept reference, flush-to-upload, last-into-slot removal, regrowth to a new array and the 16-slot pool, and setThinInstanceMatrix was uploaded with no flush on a running scene.

The probe shows the missing instance and color buffers until markMeshRenderableDirty or rebuildSceneRenderables, and colors set before registerScene or on a late-added mesh got their buffer with no extra call.

The probe shows when fog is compiled in, that a plain scene.fog write leaves the uniforms at 0, and that in-place edits are not uploaded; the 1/2/3 mode numbers match the shader, and setFog plus rebuild wrote the uniforms.

True before build and for a runtime change followed by a move, but 'no effect until its world matrix changes' is too narrow: adding a light applied a runtime excludedMeshes change with no world-matrix change.
Enable/disable and the light-removal unlink hold, but 'redrawn only when a caster or the light moves' is too narrow: a setLightIntensity change with nothing moving also redrew the map.

The probe shows the silent cap at 16 and setMaxLights before build; called after registerScene, the shaders kept array<LightEntry, 16> even after rebuildSceneRenderables, which bears out 'call before this'.
The probe shows last-registered-first order, one-callback ordering and the fixedDeltaMs override, which match onBeforeRender's unshift and the scene update code.
The probe shows framing with and without enableThinInstanceWorldBounds, scene.camera being set and no reframe for later meshes, and r04's probe shows the hidden-mesh skip.

The probe shows the name, the shared geometry and material, the clone being left out of the scene, independent retirement and the throw on a retired original; a clone not yet added also kept its buffers after the original was retired, and could still be added.
